1-1-1.graph_title: People at risk of poverty or social exclusion
1-1-1.indicator_definition: This indicator corresponds to the sum of people who are: at risk of poverty after social transfers,  severely materially and socially deprived, or living in households with very low work intensity.  Individuals are counted only once, even if they are affected by more than one of these occurrences.  People are considered at risk of poverty if their income is below 60% of the national median  equivalent disposable income.
1-1-1.rationale: Poverty and social exclusion limit people's opportunities to reach their full potential by affecting  health and reducing educational outcomes. Without effective social protection, the risk of poverty  is passed between generations, creating inequality and hindering sustainable economic growth.  The long-term objective for this indicator is a value of 0.
1-1-1.methodology_characteristics: Based on the Europe-wide harmonised annual survey on income and living conditions (EU-SILC).  From 2020 onwards, data is not strictly comparable with previous years due to methodological  revisions and integration into the microcensus.

1-3-1.graph_title: Severe material and social deprivation rate by age group and sex
1-3-1.indicator_definition: This indicator measures the proportion of the population covered by at least one social protection benefit, including benefits related to old age, disability, sickness, unemployment, family and housing. It is expressed as a percentage of the total population. Data are based on EU-SILC.
1-3-1.rationale: Effective social protection systems prevent poverty and reduce the impact of economic shocks on individuals and families. Broad coverage ensures that those in need receive timely support. Progress means extending effective coverage to all segments of the population.
1-3-1.methodology_characteristics: Data are collected from EU-SILC, which gathers information on social transfers received by households. The indicator covers both contributory (insurance-based) and non-contributory (means-tested) benefits across all categories of social protection.
